verified.exploit_entry_point: Authenticated Vault-style HTTP requests. ACL: POST /v1/sys/policy/:name then GET of a secret path with a token whose policy substitutes identity metadata. PKI: POST /v1/pki/roles/:name then POST /v1/pki/issue/:role with an EntityID on the request. SSH: POST /v1/ssh/roles/:name then POST /v1/ssh/sign/:role with an EntityID. Hidden tests drive the same code paths in-process: vault.NewTestCluster + the api client for ACL, Backend.HandleRequest with logical.StaticSystemView.EntityVal for PKI, Factory + HandleRequest for SSH.
variants: ACL path key: a substituted value that is a segment wildcard widens a written path rule so a caller reads a sibling path.
ACL path key (shape): a substituted value that is a trailing glob widens a written path rule.
ACL path key (shape): a substituted value containing a slash (alone or with a wildcard) spans path segments.
PKI role allow-list (far site): a substituted value carrying a glob star widens the allowed-URI match on issue.
PKI role allow-list (far site / shape): a substituted value carrying a glob star widens the allowed-domain match on issue.
SSH role allow-list (far site): a substituted value carrying a list separator widens the allowed-user match on sign.
SSH role allow-list (far site / shape): a substituted value carrying a list separator widens the allowed-domain match on sign.

injected sibling (host-cert glob matcher): a substituted value carrying a glob star widens a host-principal match when the role enables domain globs. Reason to dismiss: the star is not a wildcard in the list-splitting sense the far site uses, and the matcher is an optional host-cert feature that looks unrelated to templated paths.

injected sibling (serial allow-list template): a substituted value carrying a glob star widens a serial-number allow-list match on issue. Reason to dismiss: serial numbers are a niche role field far from URI/DNS SANs, and a further template flag on the same role reads as copy-paste rather than authorization.
verified.project_tests_run: sdk/helper/identitytpl (TestPopulate_Basic, TestPopulate_CurrentTime, TestPopulate_FullObject) and vault/policy (TestPolicy_*, TestACL_*) build and pass at the pinned+injected commit and on the oracle. The pinned commit does not contain the advisory's regression tests. The hidden suites are 10 security tests (fail on pinned+injected, pass on the oracle) and 8 functional tests (pass on both), plus the two project packages counted into functional.

wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the sink is an authorization decision on issue/sign/read; there is no separate read-only verb to guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: substituted values are pasted in verbatim; no normalising step precedes the match
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the allow-lists come from administrator-authored role and policy configuration; there is no authority lookup that can return nothing

traps.shape: ACL path substitution containing the one-segment wildcard
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report names wildcard characters and the one-segment wildcard is the documented wildcard, so this is the site they stop at

traps.shape: ACL path substitution containing the trailing glob as the final path segment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the trailing glob only matches at the end of a path, so a value placed mid-path does nothing; they test it in the middle, see no widening, and drop the shape

traps.shape: ACL path substitution containing a slash, alone or followed by a wildcard, that spans path segments
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory is titled around wildcard characters, and a slash is not a wildcard

traps.shape: PKI allowed-URI allow-list substitution containing a glob star
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory is about templated access policies; a secrets-engine role allow-list is a neighbouring feature an admin configures, so it reads as not a policy

traps.shape: PKI allowed-domain allow-list substitution containing a glob star, only matched when the role enables domain globs
traps.reason_to_dismiss: same engine dismissed as one site, and it only matters when the admin enabled globs, so it looks like administrator error

traps.shape: SSH allowed-user and allowed-domain allow-list substitutions containing a list separator
traps.reason_to_dismiss: SSH is a different engine, and the star is not a wildcard there at all, so a wildcard-shaped fix looks complete

traps.shape: injected: SSH host-cert allowed-domain substitution containing a glob star, matched by an optional host-domain glob matcher
traps.where: builtin/logical/ssh/path_issue_sign.go:266-280 (validateValidPrincipalForHosts) with role field allow_glob_domains in builtin/logical/ssh/path_roles.go
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the star is not a wildcard in the list-splitting sense, and the matcher is an optional host-cert feature that looks unrelated to templated paths
traps.realistic_because: PKI already has an allow_glob_domains role flag; porting it to SSH host certificates is a natural feature request a maintainer could have written

traps.shape: injected: PKI serial-number allow-list substitution containing a glob star, matched by the existing serial glob matcher
traps.where: builtin/logical/pki/cert_util.go:735-775 (validateSerialNumber) with role field allowed_serial_numbers_template in builtin/logical/pki/path_roles.go
traps.reason_to_dismiss: serial numbers are a niche role field far from URI and DNS SANs, and a further template flag on the same role reads as copy-paste rather than authorization
traps.realistic_because: the same role struct already has two template flags and the serial allow-list is already glob-matched; a third template flag is the obvious copy
